description: Pi Session commands (Follow-up / Compact / Reset / Cancel) routed to PiRuntime end-to-end, reusing the #407 command contract and OpenCode's existing behavior.

tasks.title: Verify Pi SDK command surface and extend the runtime boundary
tasks.description: Smoke-verify the pinned @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent SDK exposes the command surfaces the channels depend on: prompt preflight reception callback, session.compact(), and abort/isStreaming stop-confirmation; record findings. Extend the PiSdkSession boundary interface (runtime/pi/sdk.ts) with compact() and a prompt preflight option, and add Pi Follow-up/Cancel/Compact/Reset request+result boundary types (runtime/pi/types.ts) mirroring the OpenCode RuntimeFollowup/RuntimeCancel shapes. This delivers the boundary contract the channel tasks implement against.
acceptanceCriteria: openspec/changes/issue-451/sdk-smoke-verification.json records the verified compact() and prompt preflight signatures (or documented assumptions if the Pi environment is unavailable)
PiSdkSession exposes compact(): Promise<void> and prompt accepts a preflight reception callback option
PiFollowupRequest/Result, PiCancelRequest/Result, PiCompactRequest/Result, PiResetRequest/Result are added to packages/runner/src/runtime/pi/types.ts
npm run typecheck -w packages/runner passes with the extended boundary types
tasks.notes: If the configured Pi environment is unavailable, extend the interface from SDK type definitions and record the assumptions in the smoke file. Per design D9, escalate (do not substitute) if preflight or compact() is absent from the pinned SDK — idle-Follow-up reception confirmation and native Compact both depend on them. Precedent: openspec/changes/archive/2026-07-21-issue-450/sdk-smoke-verification.json.

tasks.title: Implement PiRuntime Follow-up and Cancel channels, with per-session prompt serialization
tasks.description: Add PiRuntime.followup and PiRuntime.cancel, plus a per-physical-session prompt mutex (design D10). followup branches on the physical session's isStreaming: busy → await session.steer(text) (projection stays owned by the active runTurn); idle → acquire the mutex, session.prompt with preflight, resolving accepted when preflight confirms reception and failing (no replay) when preflight rejects, while a background continuation holds the mutex and projects the new turn's events through an observer until prompt resolves. cancel calls session.abort() and confirms stop via isStreaming/event sequence, returning a result whose facts carry stopConfirmed (false when stop cannot be confirmed). Both surface missing-session with a Reset hint when the bound Pi session file is absent. Retrofit runTurn to acquire the same mutex so workflow turns and idle follow-ups can never issue concurrent prompts on one session.
acceptanceCriteria: A per-physical-session async mutex in PiRuntime serializes prompt calls: runTurn and the idle follow-up path both acquire it; concurrent idle follow-up + workflow turn, and two concurrent idle follow-ups, do not issue a second prompt() on the same session (fake-SDK test)

followup fake-SDK unit tests pass: busy → steer (no new turn), idle → prompt+preflight accepted on reception, idle preflight rejected → failure with no retry/replay, missing session file → missing-session + Reset hint
idle followup projects turn events through the observer until prompt resolves, then releases the mutex and tears down the subscription
cancel fake-SDK unit tests pass: abort confirmed → cancelled with stopConfirmed=true, stop unconfirmed → cancelled with stopConfirmed=false, missing session → missing-session + Reset hint
Follow-up never rotates the physical Pi Session binding (runtimeSessionId unchanged) on either branch
npm run typecheck -w packages/runner passes; npm test -w packages/runner passes
tasks.output: packages/runner/src/runtime/pi/runtime.ts with followup(), cancel(), and the per-session prompt mutex (+ unit tests in packages/runner/tests)
tasks.notes: Reuses createPiProjector, abortAndDiagnose, and resetDiagnostic helpers. Observer is a second argument to followup (request shape stays aligned with RuntimeFollowupRequest). The per-session mutex is load-bearing for the follow-up path and a redundant (safe) serialization for runTurn, which is already serialized externally by WorkflowSessionTurnCoordinator. steer does not acquire the mutex. See design D5/D6/D10.

tasks.title: Implement PiRuntime Compact and Reset channels
tasks.description: Add PiRuntime.compact and PiRuntime.reset. compact acquires the per-session prompt mutex (from T-002), guards isStreaming (→ conflict), subscribes a projector, calls session.compact() natively, returns ok with no runtimeSessionId, and on compact failure returns a failure carrying the underlying error — never synthesizes a summary or fabricates a compaction record. reset best-effort reads the current model/thinking level, calls services.createSession(workDir) for a new empty session, applies the carried model/thinking onto it, caches the new PiSdkSession under the new path, and returns the new session-file path as runtimeSessionId (the Server grain performs the binding replacement and lineage append). compact surfaces missing-session with a Reset hint; reset still succeeds when the prior session file is missing (it is the recovery operation).
acceptanceCriteria: compact acquires the per-session prompt mutex (no concurrent prompt/compact on the same physical session)

compact fake-SDK unit tests pass: native compact() invoked, runtimeSessionId unchanged after compaction, compaction events projected, compact failure → failure with no synthetic summary, busy (isStreaming) → conflict, missing session → missing-session + Reset hint

reset fake-SDK unit tests pass: new empty session created in the same workDir, current model/thinking carried over when available, returned runtimeSessionId is non-empty and differs from request.runtimeSessionId, prior session file retained for audit, missing prior session still succeeds and skips carry-over
result shapes satisfy SessionCommand validation: compact omits runtimeSessionId; reset returns a non-empty runtimeSessionId that differs from request.runtimeSessionId
npm run typecheck -w packages/runner passes; npm test -w packages/runner passes
tasks.output: packages/runner/src/runtime/pi/runtime.ts with compact() and reset() (+ unit tests in packages/runner/tests)
tasks.notes: Does not perform lineage append itself — the Server-side CompleteResetAsync commits the rebind using the returned id (existing contract). See design D7/D8.

tasks.title: Route session commands to the bound runtime end-to-end
tasks.description: Lift the Server Pi gate (AgentSessionGrain.EnsureCommandRuntimeAvailable admits pi). Thread a piRuntime accessor into RunnerSignalRClient/RunnerHost alongside openCodeRuntime and add a resolveCommandRuntime(binding) selector. Make followup-handler and cancel-handler dispatch on binding.runtime, and have RunnerHost.resolveFollowupTarget admit pi. Wire registerSessionCommandHandler into RunnerSignalRClient.registerHandlers() with a router that sends pi targets to PiRuntime.compact/reset and returns unavailable for opencode (preserving current OpenCode outcome). Surface cancel stop-confirmation honestly end-to-end: add optional interruptUnconfirmed to CancelAgentSessionReply, set it in the cancel handler when the runtime returns stopConfirmed=false, and mirror it into the cancel HTTP response. Remove the stale Pi-session-command gap entries in docs/actions/pi.md and design/runtimes/pi.md.
acceptanceCriteria: Server spec tests pass: compact, reset, follow-up, and cancel on a pi-bound session are admitted (no InvalidOperationException) and flow through the existing contract, including idle-conflict rejection, missing-binding Reset hint, and expected-binding guard for reset

Cancel honesty reaches the user: a stop-unconfirmed cancel (runtime stopConfirmed=false) produces a cancel reply/HTTP response carrying interruptUnconfirmed=true; a confirmed cancel does not; OpenCode cancel replies are unchanged (always confirmed)

Runner handler tests pass: follow-up, cancel, and SessionCommand handlers dispatch pi bindings → PiRuntime and opencode bindings → OpenCodeRuntime; regression tests assert OpenCode command outcome (result shape, error vocabulary) is unchanged

Pi compact/reset reuse the SessionCommand journal dedup by (sessionId, operationId); after a restart with a started Pi operation, an indeterminate outcome is reported via the existing vocabulary (no blind re-execute), preserving at-most-one committed effect
resolveCommandRuntime returns the existing unavailable/notStarted vocabulary for unknown or not-ready runtimes (no silent drop or synthesized success)
Routing selects the runtime from the persisted binding.runtime (a post-Reset replaced binding is honored immediately)
docs/actions/pi.md and design/runtimes/pi.md no longer list Pi session commands as unimplemented
npm test (server) passes; npm run typecheck -w packages/runner passes; npm test -w packages/runner passes
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Sessions/Grains/AgentSessionGrain.cs; packages/runner/src/server/runner-signalr.ts, runtime/host.ts, followup-handler.ts, cancel-handler.ts, session-command-handler wiring; docs/actions/pi.md, design/runtimes/pi.md
tasks.notes: OpenCode compact/reset is intentionally left as-is: through the canonical Runner-dispatched path it is already effectively Unavailable today (the runner has no SessionCommand handler; the grain's server-side summary CompactAsync has no route caller), so the opencode router branch returns unavailable immediately — same semantic outcome, no regression. Implementing real OpenCode native compact/reset on the Runner is out of scope (non-goal). See design D1–D4 and Risks.
